newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh government offloads Reckitt shares.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh government offloads Reckitt shares.

text.p: The Bangladesh government on Tuesday began selling its shares in multinational Reckitt & Colman (BD) Ltd, which is listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), government officials said.
A total of 329,000 shares will be sold through the DSE in phases by the state-owned Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (ICB), which is also an institutional investor, they said.
ICB Deputy General Manager Mohammad Jahangir said some 20,000 shares will be offered on the floor on Tuesday. The 10-taka Reckitt & Colman share sold at 450 taka ($11) on Monday.

Reckitt & Colman is the fourth company the government has divested its stake in over a three-month period. Earlier it sold shares in Bangladesh Tobacco Company Ltd (BTC), Eastern Cables Ltd and Osmania Glass Sheet Factory Ltd.

Bangladesh's Privatisation Board announced this month the government would offload shares in 15 public firms, including three multinationals, by next June. Jahangir said the government was trying to raise the supply of shares.

After BTC and Reckitt Colman, officials said, the government was preparing to sell shares in two other multinational companies -- Berger (Bangladesh) Ltd and Siemens Ltd -- and some seven banks. Siemens Ltd is the local unit of Siemens AG
